See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Minimum final score = max[(Course pass − Current × (1 − Weight / 100)) ÷ (Weight / 100), Exam minimum]

A worked example

With an 80% current grade, a 50% course threshold and a 40%-weight final, the weighted-average target alone needs 5% on the exam. If the exam must separately be passed at 40%, the actual minimum is 40%.

Before you use the result

Use the actual thresholds in your syllabus. The current grade excludes the final. This calculator combines two mathematical conditions only; it does not model attendance, minimum component scores or compulsory submissions. A result over 100% is unattainable on a standard capped exam.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Why is this different from the ordinary final calculator?

Some courses require a minimum final-exam score even when the overall weighted course average is already high enough.

Can a course still be failed after meeting this result?

Yes, if there are other requirements. Check the complete syllabus rather than relying on these two thresholds alone.
